title: Michigan's 2nd Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Michigan's 2nd Congressional District covers 20 counties in central and western Michigan, including outer portions of the Grand Rapids metropolitan area. Incumbent Republican John Moolenaar, first elected in 2014 and re-elected with 65.1% of the vote in 2024, is seeking re-election in a district rated as 'Solid Republican' by The Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball. The Democratic primary on August 4, 2026 features three candidates—Marine veteran Ben Ambrose, physician assistant Jamie Hill, and Lake County Commissioner Clyde Welford—who will compete to advance to the general election. No opinion polls for this race have been published as of mid-2026, reflecting the district's safe Republican classification.
polling_note: No opinion polls were found for Michigan's 2nd Congressional District in the 2026 cycle. Multiple nonpartisan election forecasters rate the race as 'Solid/Safe Republican.'

candidates.name: John Moolenaar
candidates.summary: John Moolenaar is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Michigan's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2014. He serves as Chairman of the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and as a member of the House Appropriations Committee, and previously served in the Michigan House of Representatives and Michigan Senate.

candidates.name: Ben Ambrose
candidates.summary: Ben Ambrose is a Marine Corps veteran and federal policy advisor running for Congress in Michigan's 2nd District. He grew up on a farm in Hesperia, served nearly 20 years in the Marine Corps as an infantryman with multiple combat tours, and has led federal innovation efforts for the Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Defense. He holds a BA from Georgetown University and an MBA from Johns Hopkins University.

candidates.name: Clyde Welford
candidates.summary: Clyde Welford is a Lake County Commissioner and retired educator running for Congress in Michigan's 2nd District. He served 35 years as a teacher, including 29 years in Baldwin Community Schools, and was elected Lake County Commissioner in 2020. Welford holds degrees from Grand Valley State University and Ferris State University, and has served as a Village of Baldwin Trustee.

forecast.rationale: No opinion polls have been published for this race, reducing confidence. However, non-polling indicators strongly favor Republicans: incumbent John Moolenaar has held the seat since 2014, was re-elected with 65.1% of the vote in 2024, and the district is rated 'Solid Republican' by Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball. The Democratic primary (August 4, 2026) is contested among three candidates—Ben Ambrose, Jamie Hill, and Clyde Welford—while Moolenaar is a well-funded incumbent with high institutional support. Based on the heavy Republican lean of the district and the incumbent's strong electoral history, a Republican win is overwhelmingly likely, though the complete absence of polling data prevents 'high' confidence.
